summary: Armand-Pierre Caussin de Perceval was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He served as professor of modern Arabic at INALCO from 1821, professor of Arabic at the Collège de France from 1833, and held a post at the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres from 1849.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a historian. Educated at the Athenaeum and the University of Göttingen (PhD 1779–1784) under Christian Gottlob Heyne, he taught at Göttingen as Privatdozent, professor of philosophy (1794), and professor of history (1801).

Arnold J. Toynbee was a historian who studied at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford. He held posts at King's College London (~1919–1924), Chatham House as director (~1925–1955), and the London School of Economics (~1925–1955).

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Tübingen, Oxford, and Leipzig (PhD ~1883) under Benfey, Roth, and Müller. He served at Oxford as Deputy Professor and later Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1888/1899–1926).

Arthur Berriedale Keith was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Royal High School, the University of Edinburgh under Julius Eggeling, and Balliol College, Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served as professor at Edinburgh from 1914 to 1944.

Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bedford School and King's College London, learning under Michael Viggo Fausbøll, Theodor Goldstücker, and Heinrich August Jäschke. He worked in the Indian Civil Service from ~1860 to 1880.

Arthur Emanuel Christensen was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and under Friedrich Carl Andreas, later holding the first chair of Oriental studies at Copenhagen from 1919 to 1945.
Arthur F. Buehler is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held a post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Arthur F. Wright was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank. He served on the faculty at Stanford from 1947 (professor in 1958) before becoming Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale in 1959.

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was a historian and Indologist who studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He served as professor at SOAS (1957–1965) and head of Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (~1965–1978).

Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Pari Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Ernestinum Gotha, Göttingen, Berlin (under Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Böckh, and Friedrich August Wolf), and Jena (PhD ~1813). He held a teaching post at the University of Berlin from ~1820 to 1831.

Arthur Venis was an Indologist educated at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Professor of English (1881) and Principal (1885) at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and taught post-Vedic Sanskrit at the University of Allahabad (~1888–1914).

Arthur Waley was a scholar of sinology and japanology. Educated at Rugby School and King's College, Cambridge, he studied under Gustav Haloun, Laurence Binyon, and Hidetsugu Yagi, and worked at the British Museum (1913–1929) and SOAS (1948).

Arthur William Ryder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Berlin, and Leipzig (PhD 1901) under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as instructor at Harvard (1902–1906) and professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1906–1938).
Arthur Woollgar Verrall studied at Wellington College (~1865–1869) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1869–1873).

Arti Dhand is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Calgary and McGill University, and became Associate Professor in the Department for the Study of Religion at the University of Toronto (~2002).
Aruna Haldar was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Kedar Nath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose, and taught at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Mumbai (PhD) under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt and at MS University of Baroda, where he taught Sanskrit (~1951–1980) and directed the Oriental Institute (1975–1981).

Arvind Sharma is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Allahabad, Syracuse University, and Harvard Divinity School, and held posts at the University of Queensland, University of Sydney, and McGill University (Birks Chair, 1994).
